summary.title: An OpenCV barcode and QR code scanner with ZBar
summary.one_liner: You learn to decode barcodes and QR codes in single images and live video with OpenCV and the ZBar library (via pyzbar in Python), including a Raspberry Pi deployment.
keywords: read qr codes in real time
takeaways: OpenCV has no dedicated barcode decoder; it handles image and video input and display, while ZBar (via pyzbar) does the decoding.
Install the zbar system library (apt libzbar0 or brew zbar) and then pip install pyzbar for Python 3.
pyzbar.decode returns each barcode's bounding rectangle, data bytes and type, which you decode to UTF-8 and draw with OpenCV.
A real-time script reads frames from a video stream and writes each unique barcode with a timestamp to a CSV file, using a set to skip duplicates.
On a Raspberry Pi with a PiCamera, the scanner ran in real time; the author found 1-D barcodes harder than QR codes and noted autofocus helps.
summary.summary: The post explains that OpenCV cannot decode barcodes by itself, so it pairs OpenCV for image handling with the ZBar library through the pyzbar Python bindings. It walks through installing zbar and pyzbar on Ubuntu, Raspbian, or macOS, then builds a single-image scanner that draws bounding boxes and labels on detected codes. A second script applies the same logic to a threaded video stream and logs unique barcodes to a CSV file. The author closes by testing the scanner on a Raspberry Pi with a PiCamera, reporting mixed results across QR codes and 1-D barcodes.
